note: Very faint CME first seen to the East in SOHO LASCO C2 beginning at 2025-10-01T07:24Z as well as by SOHO LASCO C3 and STEREO A COR2 in later frames. The source of this event is a minor eruption from AR 14240 (N16E65) as seen alongside field line opening and brightening in GOES SUVI 195.

cmeAnalyses.note: Measurement based on approximate source location and best fit between SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and STEREO A COR2. This event is too faint to track in GOES CCOR-1.

note: CME first seen in the SW by SOHO LASCO C2 beginning at 2025-10-01T10:24Z, as well as by SOHO LASCO C3, STEREO A COR2 and GOES CCOR-1 in later frames. The source of this event is a filament eruption that began lifting off from beyond the SW limb at approx. 2025-10-01T09:48Z as seen in GOES SUVI 304. This filament is also visible just along the SW limb in STEREO A EUVI 304. Field line opening can also be seen in GOES SUVI 171 and 195.

cmeAnalyses.note: BULK measurement based on approximate source location and best fit in SOHO LASCO C2/C3, STEREO A COR2 and GOES CCOR-1.
SHOCK measurement based on approximate source location and best fit in SOHO LASCO C2/C3, STEREO A COR2 and GOES CCOR-1.

note: Faint partial halo to the W in early C2 imagery, dissipating after >10 timestamps, seen (clearly) only in a couple of early timestamps in C3. Not seen in CCOR-1 bc of bad data. Super faint front could be traced in STEREO A COR2 in a couple of early timestamps. Source: M1.2 flare from AR 14226 (S09W77) and a very minor associated filament/prominence eruption seen in GOES SUVI 304 at 2025-10-02T02:24Z on the W limb, with moving/opening field lines seen near the W limb in GOES SUVI 284 at the time.

cmeAnalyses.note: Approximate analysis of this very faint (especially in STEREO A COR2) front with two coronagraphs (SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and STEREO A COR2) and based on the location of the source flare.

note: Extremely faint fuzzy front seen to the NE in early STEREO A COR2 imagery only. Source may be an eruption of one of more filaments stretching from AR 4233 (N17E03) to N of AR 4240 (centered at N35E75), seen as a series of very faint dimmings along this channel in GOES SUVI 195 after 2025-10-02T07Z. It is impossible to pinpoint the exact location of the source.

cmeAnalyses.note: The faint front of this CME is seen in STEREO A COR2 coronagraph only, and the source location is unclear, so only plane-of-sky analysis is possible.

note: This CME is visible to the east/southeast in SOHO LASCO C2/C3, GOES CCOR-1, and STEREO A COR2 imagery. The source is likely far-sided and related to a wide opening of field lines observed over the eastern limb starting around 2025-10-02T23:00Z as seen in GOES SUVI 171, 195, and 284 imagery. Faint ejecta can also be seen beyond the southeast limb around this time in GOES SUVI 304 imagery.

cmeAnalyses.note: Measurement based on the best fit between SOHO LASCO C3, GOES CCOR-1, and STEREO A COR2 imagery. As the source is far-sided and a precise source location is unknown, the measured parameters may vary slightly.

note: This CME is visible to the east in STEREO A COR2, SOHO LASCO C2/C3, and faintly in GOES CCOR-1 coronagraph imagery. The source is likely related to an M1.5 flare from Active Region 14236 (N14W12) starting around 2025-10-03T05:00Z as seen in GOES SUVI 131, 171, 195, 284, 304 and STEREO A EUVI 195 and 304 imagery. Post eruptive arcades are visible starting around 2025-10-03T06:00Z as seen in GOES SUVI 171 and 195 imagery.

cmeAnalyses.note: Measurement based on the best fit between SOHO LASCO C2 and STEREO A COR2 imagery. The measured longitude varies slightly from the source longitude, indicating possible deflection from a southwestern coronal hole.

note: Faint, wide, slow CME observed as barely a partial halo to the E/SE in SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and GOES CCOR-1, and more directly to the E in STEREO A COR2 with a large data gap between 2025-10-03T18:53Z to 2025-10-03T22:23Z. The source for this event is uncertain, and the slow evolving lobed nature of the front highlights this uncertainty, with two visible eruption candidates that are poor fits. A filament eruption spanning N20W30 to N40W60 which begins to lift-off around 2025-10-03T15:45Z as seen in GOES SUVI 131/171/195/304 is observed, along with faint, slow dimming and field line loop brightening over cluster of AR 14232 (N04W14) and AR 14236 (N10W22) starting around 2025-10-03T15:00Z; but neither source is clearly associated with this front.

cmeAnalyses.note: Triangulation between SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and STEREO A COR2 with a higher degree of uncertainty. This is due to the lack of clean observed source, faint leading edge in SOHO LASCO, a large data gap in STEREO A COR2 spanning most of this event, and the lobed front which is partially chopped off for this analysis focusing on the main equatorial lobe best viewed from COR2A. While uncertainty lies in the latitude, longitude, and half width, there is higher certainty in the speed being <=250 km/s.

note: Faint wide CME observed to the W in SOHO LASCO C2/C3, GOES CCOR-1, and two frames of STEREO A COR2 before a data gap begins at 2025-10-03T18:53Z. The source is observed well in GOES SUVI 171/195/284/304 as field line movement over the west limb beginning at 2025-10-03T16:56Z. In STEREO A EUVI 195/304, a brightening around S20W40 as viewed from STEREO A is observed starting around 2025-10-03T16:35Z, with STEREO A located around W48.3 degrees at this time.

cmeAnalyses.note: Triangulation between SOHO LASCO C2 and 2 available frames of STEREO A COR2 before its data gap. CME front diffuses out in LASCO C2 and is tricky to track in later frames and in LASCO C3.

note: This CME is visible to the northeast in SOHO LASCO C2/C3, GOES CCOR-1, and STEREO A COR2 imagery. The source is a filament eruption observed slightly beyond the northeast limb starting around 2025-10-03T21:00Z as seen in GOES SUVI 131, 171, 195, 284, 304 imagery. An opening of field lines is also observed at this time in GOES SUVI 131, 171, and 195 imagery.

cmeAnalyses.note: Measurement based on the best fit between SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and STEREO A COR2 imagery.

note: This CME is visible to the west in SOHO LASCO C2/C3, GOES CCOR-1, and STEREO A COR2 imagery. The source is likely an eruption from former Active Region 14226, which was located around 105-110 degrees longitude at the time of the eruption, starting around 2025-10-04T04:15Z as seen in STEREO A EUVI 195 and 304 imagery.

cmeAnalyses.note: Measurement based on the approximate source location and best fit between SOHO LASCO C3 and STEREO A COR2 imagery.

note: This CME is visible to the northeast in STEREO A COR2. It is not observed in SOHO LASCO C2/C3 or GOES CCOR-1 imagery. The source is likely far-sided as there are no source signatures on the Earth or STEREO A-facing disk around the time of this event.

cmeAnalyses.note: A plane-of-sky measurement was made using a longitude of -42 degrees as this event is only observed in STEREO A COR2 imagery and the source location is unknown.

note: This CME is visible to the northwest in SOHO LASCO C2/C3, GOES CCOR-1, and STEREO A COR2 imagery. The source is likely far-sided and related to an eruption observed near the western limb in STEREO A EUVI 304 imagery starting around 2025-10-04T13:45Z.

cmeAnalyses.note: Measurement based on the best fit between SOHO LASCO C2 and STEREO A COR2 imagery.

note: CME observed to the W in SOHO LASCO C2/C3, GOES CCOR-1, and STEREO A COR2; first of 2 concurrent fronts from what appears to be the same source eruption, preceeding the wider but more faint CME: 2025-10-04T17:24Z. The source is west limb far-sided field line breaking observed in GOES SUVI 171/195/284/304 starting around 2025-10-04T16:45Z, also observed in STEREO A EUVI 195/304 around 2025-10-04T16:25Z as field line breaking and brief brightening around S08W70/S08W80 as viewed from STEREO A (located at W48.3 at eruption time).

cmeAnalyses.note: Triangulation between SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and STEREO A COR2.

note: CME observed to the W in SOHO LASCO C2 and STEREO A COR2 as it fades before becoming visible in SOHO LASCO C3 and GOES CCOR-1; second of two concurrent fronts from what appears to be the same source eruption, following the brighter and more thin CME: 2025-10-04T17:12Z. The source is west limb far-sided field line breaking observed in GOES SUVI 171/195/284/304 starting around 2025-10-04T16:45Z, also observed in STEREO A EUVI 195/304 around 2025-10-04T16:25Z as field line breaking and brief brightening around S08W70/S08W80 as viewed from STEREO A (located at W48.3 at eruption time).

cmeAnalyses.note: Triangulation between SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and STEREO A COR2.

note: Narrow CME first seen to the SE beginning at 2025-10-04T18:23Z by STEREO A COR2. CME is not clearly seen in SOHO LASCO C2/C3 or GOES CCOR-1. The source of this event is a filament eruption seen along the SE limb (S18E80) beginning at approx. 2025-10-04T17:05Z with liftoff occurring at approx. 2025-10-04T17:49Z as seen in GOES SUVI 304. Field line opening is also visible in GOES SUVI 195.

cmeAnalyses.note: Single spacecraft measurement based on approximate source location and best fit in STEREO A COR2.

note: Faint CME observed to the NE in SOHO LASCO C2/C3, GOES CCOR-1, and STEREO A COR2. The source is a small filament eruption from AR 14243 centered around N23E44, observed in GOES SUVI 171/195/284/304 as filament ejecta, field line movement, and brightening on-disk starting at 2025-10-04T21:56Z.

cmeAnalyses.note: Triangulation between SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and STEREO A COR2.

note: Faint CME first seen to the West by SOHO LASCO C2 beginning at 2025-10-05T06:24Z, as well as by STEREO A COR2 in later frames. The source of this event is an eruption from beyond the West limb, with post-eruptive arcades seen in STEREO A EUVI 195 visually estimated to be located at approx. S05W100. Field line opening is also visible in GOES SUVI 195 along the West limb.

cmeAnalyses.note: Measurement based off of approximate source location and best fit between SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and STEREO A COR2.

note: CME observed to the NW in SOHO LASCO C2/C3, GOES CCOR-1, and STEREO A COR2. Source is not clear, and may be a tiny filament ejecta over the NW limb observed only in a few frames of GOES SUVI 304 starting around 2025-10-06T01:57Z

cmeAnalyses.note: Triangulation between SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and STEREO A COR2.

note: Faint CME observed to the SW in SOHO LASCO C2/C3, GOES CCOR-1, and STEREO A COR2, seen better the further into the FOV it travels. No observable source on disk; the CME front seems to materialize in LASCO C2 and STEREO A COR2 FOV and become better defined as it travels.

cmeAnalyses.note: Triangulation between SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and STEREO A COR2, with some difficulty due to faintness of the CME front.

note: Faint wide CME observed to the W in SOHO LASCO C2 and STEREO A COR2. The source is likely a far-sided eruption, with two brief filament ejections that largely fall back to the disk starting around 2025-10-06T08:57Z and 2025-10-06T09:01Z in GOES SUVI 304, observed as wider field line opening in SUVI 171/195/304. Also observed in STEREO A EUVI 195 starting at 2025-10-06T08:55Z and EUVI 304 at 2025-10-06T09:45Z roughly around S10W70-S10W80 as viewed from STEREO A (located at W48.4 degrees at eruption time).

cmeAnalyses.note: Triangulation between STEREO A COR2 with better visibility, and faint observations in SOHO LASCO C2. Source could range W150-W160.

note: CME seen to the NE in SOHO LASCO C2/C3, STEREO A COR2, and GOES CCOR-1. Associated with a narrow filament eruption that partially escapes from the Sun seen off the northeast limb around 2025-10-06T12:00Z seen best in GOES SUVI 304.

cmeAnalyses.note: Leading edge measurement out to nine solar radii when the CME becomes so diffuse it is unable to be measured.

note: Relatively narrow CME seen to the west-northwest in SOHO LASCO C2 and either not seen in STEREO A COR2A or is seen as a wider event to the west despite narrow width in C2. Not clearly visible in GOES CCOR-1. May be continued outflow of clearly far-sided activity that has occurred in the last few days, but it is difficult to ascertain with available imagery.

cmeAnalyses.note: Leading edge plane of sky measurement using only available imagery from SOHO LASCO C2; the CME is not well seen in SOHO LASCO C3 or STEREO A COR2.

note: Bright CME first seen to the SE in STEREO A COR2 beginning at 2025-10-07T07:09Z, as well as by GOES CCOR-1 and SOHO LASCO C2/C3 in later frames. The source of this event is a slow erupting filament beginning at approx. 2025-10-07T05:21Z located near AR 14244 (S21E46), although is likely deflected due to its proximity to a large coronal hole. This filament is seen clearly in GOES SUVI and STEREO A EUVI 304, along with field line opening visible in GOES SUVI 284 and STEREO A EUVI 195.

cmeAnalyses.note: Measurement based on approximate source location and best fit between STEREO A COR2 and GOES CCOR-1.

note: Narrow CME seen due south in SOHO LASCO C2 and not seen in STEREO A COR at the time of analysis due to a data gap; the CME may potentially be associated with a minor filament eruption located on the Earth-facing disk near 2025-10-07T14:00Z around S45W20 with southern deflection, though confidence is relatively low with currently available imagery.

cmeAnalyses.note: Plane-of-sky measurement of faint leading edge using three frames of SOHO LASCO C2 and three frames of SOHO LASCO C3, since there is still no STEREO A COR2 imagery is available for this CME and because confidence in the source is so low.
Speculative one spacecraft measurement assuming that the CME source location is relatively near S45W20 as determine by available EUV imagers.

note: Extremely faint and narrow CME seen to the NW in SOHO LASCO C2 and GOES CCOR-1, and to the NE in STEREO A COR2. Source is a subtle area of opening field lines seen around N40W30 (no AR) in GOES SUVI 284 starting around 2025-10-07T20:36Z. This CME becomes diffuse before reaching the SOHO LASCO C3 field of view.

cmeAnalyses.note: Best fit measurement of extremely faint leading edge using a few frames of SOHO LASCO C2, STEREO A COR2, and GOES CCOR-1, before the leading edge becomes completely diffuse in all three coronagraphs. The leading edge becomes diffuse before reaching the SOHO LASCO C3 field of view.

note: This CME is faint but visible to the northwest in GOES CCOR-1 and to the northeast in STEREO A COR2 imagery. The source is likely related to an eruption from former Active Region, now plage region, 14240 (N20W30) starting around 2025-10-08T08:00Z as seen in GOES SUVI and STEREO A EUVI 195 and 304 imagery. Faint dimming can be observed in GOES SUVI 195 imagery near the eruption site, and minor field line movement is observed over the northwest limb around this time in GOES SUVI 284 imagery.

cmeAnalyses.note: Measurement based on the approximate source location and best fit between GOES CCOR-1 and STEREO A COR2 imagery.

note: Narrow, asymmetric CME seen to the southeast in SOHO LASCO C2, STEREO A COR2A, and GOES CCOR1 and not seen in SOHO LASCO C3 as it is blocked by the pylon first seen at 2025-10-08T16:00Z in SOHO LASCO C2; the CME is likely associated with a prominence eruption seen on the southeast limb near 2025-10-08T15:25Z best seen in GOES SUVI 304.

cmeAnalyses.note: Leading edge measurement using triangulation between SOHO LASCO C2 and STEREO A COR2 to approximate the longitude; the measurement suggests some westward deflection relative to the source.

note: CME visible to the NE in SOHO LASCO C2/C3, STEREO A COR2, and GOES CCOR-1. The source is an eruption from near AR 14246 (approx. N25E35), which has decayed to plage. The eruption is best seen as dimming in GOES-P SUVI 195 starting at 2025-10-09T05:16Z. The eruption is also seen as moving/opening field lines off the NE limb from the point of view of STEREO A EUV 195 imagery.

cmeAnalyses.note: Measurement based on source location as well as the best fit between SOHO LASCO C2/C3, STEREO A COR2, and GOES CCOR-1 imagery in SWPC_CAT.

note: CME visible to the west in SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and GOES CCOR-1. Not clearly visible in STEREO A COR2. The source is an M2.0 flare and eruption from approximately N05W95, best seen on the limb in GOES SUVI 131 imagery and on the NW quadrant of the disk from the point of view of STEREO A EUV 195. The source is likely former AR 14236 (N05W95) which rotated off of the Earth-facing disk on 2025-10-08.

cmeAnalyses.note: Measurement based on source location with the best fit between SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and GOES CCOR-1 imagery in SWPC_CAT.

note: CME visible to the NE in STEREO A COR2 and faintly to the NNE in SOHO LASCO C2/C3. Not visible in GOES CCOR-1. The source is an eruption starting around 2025-10-11T01:16Z north of former AR 14246 (approximately N25E10). The eruption is best seen as dimming and moving field lines in GOES SUVI 195. The eruption is also visible near the NE limb from the point of view of STEREO A EUV 195 imagery.

cmeAnalyses.note: Measurement based on the best fit between SOHO LASCO C2 and STEREO A COR2 in SWPC_CAT. The CME is very faint in SOHO LASCO C2 and is not clearly measurable in SOHO LASCO C3.

note: CME visible to the SE in STEREO A COR2 and SOHO LASCO C2/C3. The CME is obscured by the pylon in GOES CCOR-1. The source is a filament eruption near AR 14249 (approx. S20E45) starting around 2025-10-11T08:56Z in GOES SUVI 304. Opening field lines and brightening are best seen in GOES SUVI 195. Opening field lines are also visible in GOES SUVI 171/284 and off the SE limb as seen from STEREO A EUV 195.

cmeAnalyses.note: Measurement based on the source location and the best fit between SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and STEREO A COR2. The CME appears to deflect to the west of the source location.

note: CME visible to the east in STEREO A COR2. Not clearly visible in SOHO LASCO C2/C3 or GOES CCOR-1. Partially overlaps in the field of view with CME: 2025-10-11T10:09Z. No clear source is found, and the CME may be farsided.

cmeAnalyses.note: Plane of sky measurement using STEREO A COR2 imagery only in SWPC_CAT.

note: Narrow faint jet-like CME seen to the WSW in SOHO LASCO C2 and GOES CCOR-1 but not seen in STEREO A COR2 coronagraph. Source of this event has not been found.

cmeAnalyses.note: Plane-of-sky analysis, since jet is not seen in COR2A and source has not been found.

note: Faint fuzzy front seen clearly W in SOHO LASCO C2 for a couple of early timestamps, dissipating soon, and very faintly seen in C3 and in GOES CCOR-1. Not seen at all in STEREO A COR2 coronagraph. Its source is likely a significant S-shaped filament eruption to SE of ARs 4242 & 4245 (STEREO A EUV 195/304) starting at 2025-10-11T18:05Z (and possibly a bit earlier), followed by more focused  post-eruptive arcades just SE of AR 4245 (~S15W50, as seen from STEREO A).

cmeAnalyses.note: Very uncertain, approximate analysis with SOHO LASCO, based on the approximate source location - a large filament eruption very approximately centered at (S15W100).

note: Faint CME to the ESE in SOHO LASCO C2 and GOES CCOR-1 and to the SSE in STEREO A COR2. This slightly brighter (possibly bulk) front is preceded by a very faint (possibly shock) front. This front is one of a series of consecutive, closely following, very similar fronts. Its source is likely a slow, loop-like filament eruption seen behind/near the SE limb in GOES SUVI 304 starting at 2025-10-11T18:13Z.

cmeAnalyses.note: A very approximate analysis based on the fit with two coronagraphs - SOHO LASCO and STEREO A COR2. The fit confirms that the source is far-sided, however STEREO A COR2 imagery is very fuzzy, so this analysis is somewhat speculative.

note: Slow CME seen to the NE in SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and GOES CCOR-1 and to the NNW in STEREO A COR2. Its source has not been found and is likely far-sided, tentatively related to an opening of field lines observed over the northern limb in GOES SUVI 284 imagery starting around 2025-10-12T06:30Z.

cmeAnalyses.note: Approximate analysis based on the fit with SOHO LASCO and STEREO A COR2 coronagraphs. The source is clearly far-sided.

note: This CME is visible to the south in SOHO LASCO C2/C3, GOES CCOR-1, and STEREO A COR2 imagery. The source is a far-sided filament eruption visible over the southern limb in GOES SUVI 171, 195, 284, 304 imagery which begins to lift off around 2025-10-12T07:40Z. An associated opening of field lines can be seen around this time in GOES SUVI 284 imagery. This eruption is also seen in STEREO A EUVI 195 and 304 imagery from beyond the western limb.

cmeAnalyses.note: Measurement based on the best fit between SOHO LASCO C2, GOES CCOR-1, and STEREO A COR2 imagery.

note: Slow CME following the 2025-10-12T07:48Z CME and seen to the NE in SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and GOES CCOR-1 and to the NNW in STEREO A COR2. Its source has not been found, so it is likely far-sided.

cmeAnalyses.note: Approximate analysis based on the fit with SOHO LASCO and STEREO A COR2 coronagraphs. The source is clearly far-sided.

note: This CME is visible to the north/northwest in SOHO LASCO C2 and GOES CCOR-1 imagery, and to the northeast in STEREO A COR2 imagery. The source is likely an eruption observed from the vicinity of Active Region 14246 (N25W15) starting around 2025-10-12T13:30Z as seen in GOES SUVI 131, 171, 195, 284, 304 imagery. Dimming is seen in GOES SUVI 195 and STEREO A EUVI 195 imagery.

cmeAnalyses.note: Measurement based on the approximate source location, accounting for deflection from a nearby coronal hole, and the best fit between SOHO LASCO C2 and STEREO A COR2 imagery.

note: CME seen to the NE in STEREO A COR2 only and likely not seen in SOHO LASCO and GOES CCOR-1 coronagraphs, possibly since it overlaps with a couple of preceding CMEs. Its source could be the C9.6 flare in AR 4246 (N22W10) and an associated eruption with dimming to the SE of this Active Region best seen in STEREO A EUV 195, but also seen in GOES SUVI 131, 171, 195, 284, 304 imagery. The CME partially overlaps with the more northern, 2025-10-12T14:23Z CME which may be associated with the dimming to the NW of this Active Region.

cmeAnalyses.note: Very uncertain one-coronagraph (STEREO A COR2) analysis of this CME based on the flare in AR 4246 as the (rather speculative) source of this CME. Because the front is not detectable in SOHO LASCO and GOES CCOR-1 imagery and the CME overlaps with two other CMEs, and due to the fact that the flare is accompanied by a very complex-shape dimming this analysis is very approximate.

note: CME visible to the NE in SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and GOES CCOR-1. Not clearly visible in STEREO A COR2. The source was not found, and the CME may be farsided.

cmeAnalyses.note: Plane of sky measurement using SOHO LASCO C2/C3 running difference imagery in SWPC_CAT.

note: Faint CME seen to the west in SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and to the east in STEREO A COR2. Not clearly visible in GOES CCOR-1 imagery. The source is likely a C9.3 flare and eruption from AR 14246 (N24W12) best seen in GOES SUVI 131. The eruption is also visible with brightening in GOES SUVI 195 and STEREO A EUV 195.

cmeAnalyses.note: Measurement based on source location as well as the best fit between SOHO LASCO C2 and STEREO A COR2 imagery. The leading edge is not clearly measurable in SOHO LASCO C3 or GOES CCOR-1, and this measurement is based on limited imagery. Due to the faintness of the leading edge, this measurement is more approximate than usual.

note: CME visible to the NW in SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and GOES CCOR-1 and to the NE in STEREO A COR2. The source is an M1.9 flare peaking at 2025-10-13T05:26Z from AR 14246 (N24W19). The flare is best seen in GOES SUVI 131 and eruption with dimming and opening field lines is best seen in GOES SUVI 195. The eruption is also visible in STEREO A EUV imagery.

cmeAnalyses.note: Measurement with updated imagery based on SOHO LASCO C2/C3, STEREO A COR2, and GOES CCOR-1 imagery.

Preliminary measurement based on source location using STEREO A COR2 imagery only. There is a real-time gap in SOHO imagery and the leading edge of the CME is difficult to track in GOES CCOR-1 running difference imagery.

note: Wide CME visible to the NE in STEREO A COR2 and the NW in SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and STEREO A COR2. The source is an M1.2 flare from AR 14246 (N24W23) peaking at 2025-10-13T13:18Z. Eruption with dimming and opening field lines best seen in GOES SUVI 195 and from the point of view of STEREO A EUV 195.

cmeAnalyses.note: Measurement based primarily on GOES CCOR-1 and STEREO A COR2 imagery, with one frame of SOHO LASCO C3 imagery available.

note: CME first seen to the ENE in SOHO LASCO C2 around 2025-10-13T17:00Z slightly to the north of a narrow but bright streamer. This narrow CME is also seen to the ENE in SOHO LASCO C3 and to the NE in STEREO A COR2 but is not seen in GOES CCOR-1. There is not a good source candidate on the Earth-facing disk, so the source is likely far-sided. This is supported by a slightly far-sided measurement.

cmeAnalyses.note: Measurement based on best-fit between SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and STEREO A COR2.

note: CME first seen to the E in SOHO LASCO C2 starting at 2025-10-13T23:36Z. This CME is only seen in SOHO LASCO C2. The source of this CME is possibly a small amount of ejecta from beyond the E limb best seen in GOES SUVI 304 starting around 2025-10-13T23:05Z. The leading edge is very faint and fades quickly.

cmeAnalyses.note: Preliminary plane-of-sky measurement based on running difference imagery from SOHO LASCO C2.

note: Bright CME seen to the E in all three coronagraphs, followed by two also very bright fronts, one with H-alpha emission. This could be the shock front of a two-lobed CME (the two following fronts being bulk fronts). Its source is the large prominence eruption on/close to the NE limb starting to lift off around 2025-10-14T00:00Z, as seen in GOES SUVI 304 (starting to rise around 2025-10-13T23:00Z), with massive post-eruptive arcades seen in SUVI 304 and 195 centered around N25E70.

cmeAnalyses.note: Analysis based on the fit of the front with two coronagraphs (SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and STEREO A COR2) and somewhat confirmed by the approximate location of the post-eruptive arcades (N25E70).

Analysis of this (secondary, likely bulk) bright front following the possible shock front, based on the fit with two coronagraphs (SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and STEREO A COR2), confirmed by the approximate location of the post-eruptive arcades following the filament eruption.

N30W80) in GOES SUVI and STEREO A EUVI 304 beginning at 2025-10-14T20:09Z, along with field line opening seen in GOES SUVI 284.

cmeAnalyses.note: Measurement based on the best fit between SOHO LASCO C2/C3, GOES CCOR-1, and STEREO A COR2 imagery as well as source location.

note: Bright flux rope CME seen to the NW in SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and GOES CCOR-1, and to the NNW in STEREO A COR2. The source is the combined effects of two eruptions from AR 14246 (N25W80) which occur in close succession. The first eruption from AR 14246 (N25W80) is characterized by a small loop of ejecta seen lifting off at or near AR 14246 (N25W80) starting at 2025-10-17T10:57Z in GOES SUVI 304 and very widely opening field lines from the same location seen in GOES SUVI 284. Brightening and opening field line movement can be seen from AR 14246 in STEREO A EUVI 304 imagery. The second eruption from AR 14246 (N25W80), which includes an M1.1 flare, is characterized by a much more rapid instance of opening field lines seen in GOES SUVI 284 starting at 2025-10-17T12:37Z, and brightening and ejecta seen starting at 2025-10-17T12:45Z in STEREO A EUVI 304 imagery. Both instances of opening field lines likely resulted in two leading edges, which may have combined so early in their propagation that they appear as one leading edge by the time they appear in the SOHO LASCO C2 field of view.

cmeAnalyses.note: Measurement using source location seen in available UV imagery and best fit between several frames of SOHO LASCO C2/C3, STEREO A COR2, and GOES CCOR-1.

A wide region of dimming stretching towards the South and West can be seen in SDO AIA 193 and 211, along with field line opening seen in SDO AIA 171 and GOES SUVI 284.

cmeAnalyses.note: Measurement based on approximate source location and best fit in SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and GOES CCOR-1. STEREO A COR2 was not available for this measurement.

cmeAnalyses.note: Measurement based on source location. This measurement uses limited available SOHO LASCO C2 imagery due to the CME's faintness.

note: CME seen to the east in GOES CCOR-1 and SOHO LASCO C2/C3. The CME is not seen in STEREO A COR2. The source is not found, and the CME is likely farsided.

note: Faint, high Northern latitude CME with a loop-like front seen to the N in all three coronagraphs but best seen in running difference imagery. cmeAnalyses.note: Approximate analysis based on the fit of the faint front of this CME with all three coronagraphs (SOHO LASCO C2/C3, STEREO A COR2 and GOES CCOR-1). No clear source has been found to confirm this measurement.

note: Faint CME with a loop-like front seen to the W in SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and GOES CCOR-1 coronagraphs and not seen in STEREO A COR2 coronagraph. A faint but distinct source is likely a minor eruption W of Active Region 14317, centered around (N10W50), happening over 2025-12-29T08Z-11Z and seen as minor dimming and faint but high-rising post-eruptive arcades, as seen in SDO AIA 195 and GOES SUVI 284.

cmeAnalyses.note: One-coronagraph (SOHO LASCO and GOES CCOR-1) analysis based on the likely (but rather faint) source: eruption W of AR 14317. The CME front is not seen in STEREO A COR2, so this analysis cannot be corroborated by triangulation.

note: CME seen to the southeast in SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and GOES CCOR-1. Not clearly visible in STEREO A COR2. The source is likely an eruption best seen starting around 2025-12-29T15:04Z in SDO AIA 193, around S20E75, characterized by dimming and opening field lines.

cmeAnalyses.note: Measurement based on source location using SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and GOES CCOR-1 running difference imagery in SWPC_CAT.

note: This CME is visible to the west in SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and GOES CCOR-1 imagery. This event is not seen in STEREO A COR2 imagery in real-time due to a data gap starting at 2025-12-29T16:53Z. The source is an eruption centered near S10W63 starting around 2025-12-29T19:40Z seen in SDO AIA 131/171/193/304 imagery and GOES SUVI 131/171/195/284/304 imagery. cmeAnalyses.note: Measurement based on the source longitude. A triangulated measurement was not available due to a data gap in STEREO A COR2 imagery at the time of this event. The measured parameters may vary slightly as a result.

note: Very faint CME seen to the SE in SOHO LASCO C2/C3, GOES CCOR-1, and faintly to the SE in STEREO A COR2. Best seen in running difference imagery. The CME later overlaps with multiple eastern CME fronts, so analysis is not straightforward. One potential source could be a minor eruption in the newly numbered AR 14331 (S25E61) seen starting at 2025-12-30T06:00Z in SDO AIA/GOES SUVI 304, with ejecta directed southwardly, however the fit with three coronagraphs (SOHO LASCO C2/C3, STEREO A COR2 and GOES CCOR-1) strongly indicates a far-sided source. In addition to the brigher, dimpled bulk, there is a much fainter and wider shock, mostly seen to the S.

cmeAnalyses.note: Approximate analysis based on the fit of the faint dimpled front with three coronagraphs (SOHO LASCO C2/C3, STEREO A COR2 and GOES CCOR-1). No coronal signatures of a far-sided source seen in EUV imagery.

note: Faint CME seen to the NE in all three coronagraphs (SOHO LASCO C2/C3, STEREO A COR2 and GOES CCOR-1), with the faint front quickly becoming fuzzy/partially dissipating. The CME is somewhat overlapping with the more southern CME: 2025-12-30T07:00Z. A possible source is a narrow prominence/ejecta rotating northwardly seen starting at 2025-12-30T06:49Z in GOES SUVI 304 (and SDO AIA 304) on/behind the E limb (lat -15), however the fit between coronagraphs shows a much lower longitude, indicating AR 14324 (N25W33) as a possible source. There is a C3.5-class flare in this Active Region at the time.

cmeAnalyses.note: Analysis based on the fit with three coronagraphs (SOHO LASCO C2/C3, STEREO A COR2 and GOES CCOR-1) and including the northern portion of this fuzzy, dimpled front. Takes into account later timeframes of coronagraphs. Possible source is the C class flare from Active Region 14324.
Very preliminary analysis based on the fit with three coronagraphs (SOHO LASCO C2/C3, STEREO A COR2 and GOES CCOR-1).

note: A CME to the ESE, with the front clearest in STEREO A COR2 coronagraph and super faint in SOHO and GOES CCOR-1. No clear source has been found it could potentially be an impulsive C5.0 flare from Active Region 14325 (S09E27) peaking at 2025-12-30T06:45Z. There is one bright post-eruptive arcade after the flare as well, but no other coronal signatures.

cmeAnalyses.note: A very speculative analysis based on the fit of fronts in two coronagraphs (relatively clear front in STEREO A COR2 and a super faint partial halo front in SOHO LASCO C2 coronagraph). Not confirmed by a clear source, but there is an impulsive flare from Active Region 14325 at the time that fits the bill.

note: Faint, less than 10 degree half-width CME observed to the NNW in SOHO LASCO C2/C3, GOES CCOR-1, and STEREO A COR2. The source may be field line movement and filament activity on the farside, viewed only in low-cadence STEREO A EUVI 195 and EUVI 304 imagery starting around 2025-12-30T09:35Z on the west limb as viewed from STEREO A, putting this source around W140.

Eruption also observed as brightening on disk and field line movement in SDO AIA 171/193/304.

cmeAnalyses.note: Single spacecraft 3D analysis with SOHO LASCO C2/C3 as STEREO A COR2 imagery not available for this CME, using the flare source of S17E42 as the longitude. As such, the longitude could easily vary E30-E50 if deflection occurred.

note: CME visible to the NW in SOHO LASCO C2/C3, GOES CCOR-1, and STEREO A COR2.
